questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Miranda said to her teacher, "I was sick for a day."

options.text: Miranda told her teacher that she has been sick for a day.
Miranda told her teacher that she is sick for a day.
Miranda told her teacher that she was sick for a day.
Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** correct indirect form **of the sentence *"Miranda said to her teacher, 'I was sick for a day.'*" **is** *"Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day."*
 
• When converting direct speech into indirect speech, the tense of the verbs usually shifts back (this is known as "backshifting").
 
• In this case, the** past simple tense** "was" **changes to **the past perfect tense "had been."
 
• This shift accurately conveys the timing of the events in the indirect speech.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *'Miranda told her teacher that she had been sick for a day.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Miranda told her teacher that she has been sick for a day." **- This is incorrect because the present perfect "has been" doesn't accurately convey the timing of past events in indirect speech.
 
• **"Miranda told her teacher that she is sick for a day."** - This is incorrect because the present tense "is" doesn't accurately represent the past events conveyed in the original direct speech.
 
• **"Miranda told her teacher that she was sick for a day." **- Although it might seem correct in some contexts, in proper English grammar, while changing from direct to indirect speech, the tense usually shifts back. Therefore, "was" should become "had been."

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.

P. In July 1977, Marley was found to have a type of malignant melanoma (cancer) under the nail of a toe.

Q. He died on 11 May 1981 at Cedars of Lebanon Hospital in Miami (now University of Miami Hospital) at the age of 36 .

R. Despite his illness, he continued touring until his health deteriorated as the cancer had spread throughout his body.

S. Marley turned down his doctors' advice to have his toe amputated, citing his religious beliefs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct order **of these sentences is indeed** PSRQ,** which tells a coherent and chronological story about Marley's illness and death.
 
• **Here's the reasoning:**
 
• **P. **"In July 1977, Marley was found to have a type of malignant melanoma (cancer) under the nail of a toe." -** This sentence is logically first** as it introduces the subject of Marley's illness.
 
• **S. "**Marley turned down his doctors' advice to have his toe amputated, citing his religious beliefs." - **This sentence logically follows P** because it describes Marley's response to his diagnosis.
 
• **R. **"Despite his illness, he continued touring until his health deteriorated as the cancer had spread throughout his body." -** This sentence follows S,** describing what happened after Marley declined the recommended medical treatment.
 
• **Q. **"He died on 11 May 1981 at Cedars of Lebanon Hospital in Miami (now University of Miami Hospital) at the age of 36." - **This sentence logically concludes** the sequence, giving the final result of Marley's illness.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** reads:* "In July 1977, Marley was found to have a type of malignant melanoma (cancer) under the nail of a toe. Marley turned down his doctors' advice to have his toe amputated, citing his religious beliefs. Despite his illness, he continued touring until his health deteriorated as the cancer had spread throughout his body. He died on 11 May 1981 at Cedars of Lebanon Hospital in Miami (now University of Miami Hospital) at the age of 36." This sequence (PSRQ) is therefore the correct answer.*
